- When sentiment is consistently negative or neutral over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward — reduce forecast bias by 5–10% below historical mean.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior 30d), model often overshoots and fails to mean-revert — cap forecast peak at 1.5x prior high or adjust downward by 2–3% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- If sentiment is positive and price is trending up, model frequently overestimates momentum — reduce forecast slope by 10–20% if sentiment >0.67 for 3+ consecutive days.
- When sentiment is mixed or volatile, model exhibits lagged response — delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days if sentiment swings >0.33 in magnitude.
- If true outcome is consistently below forecast (e.g., 3+ consecutive days), model may be overconfident — apply downward bias of 1–3% per day if sentiment remains flat or negative.
- For 30d horizon, model often underestimates short-term volatility — increase forecast variance by 10–15% if sentiment is volatile or recent price action is erratic.
